evals.prompt: I run Kestrel Systems' annual developer conference, about 600 people, and we have three things happening Wednesday 19:00-22:00: a beer-and-boardgames night in the hotel bar (ground floor, step-free, beer on tap), a karaoke room on the second floor reachable only by stairs with an alcohol-free bar, and a bring-your-kids pizza social on the mezzanine up a short flight of steps with beer available. Our accessibility page commits to step-free routes to every official space, an alcohol-free option, and family-inclusive evening programming. Each of the three was signed off individually by the organiser who proposed it, so I think we're fine. Sanity-check the evening and write up the social programme so we can post it Friday.
evals.expected_output: A finding that the 19:00-22:00 slot has no option clearing all three published commitments at once, the three named fixes, a refusal to publish with the gap noted, and a requirement to name which option clears the floor beside the slate.
expectations: Identifies that no single option in the 19:00-22:00 slot clears all three published commitments (step-free, alcohol-free, family-inclusive) at once
States the check as a slate-level or per-slot floor, explicitly contrasted with checking each activity on its own
States that every activity passing its own individual sign-off is precisely why the gap survived
Offers the three fixes for the failing slot: add a clearing option to that slot, move one activity out of it, or narrow the slate
Refuses to note the gap and publish the programme anyway
Requires the published slate itself to state which option clears the floor, rather than a separate page a reader finds afterwards
Names which activity is step-free, which is alcohol-free, and which is family-inclusive, using the terms of the event's own published access commitments
Hands the finished per-slot check and any uncovered slot back to the accessibility work that owns the commitments, without setting a new bar of its own
Identifies concurrency as what created the failure, noting a slate whose occasions never share an hour cannot fail this floor on choice

evals.prompt: Fernbrook Labs here. Our conference is two days and we've already locked the Thursday evening mixer, venue booked and catering signed. Day two's evening is completely empty and it feels like a waste of a slot. I was thinking we add a second thing, maybe a pub quiz or a walking tour, so people have more to do. It'd be me organising it on top of everything else, same as the mixer. Nobody has actually asked for it, I just don't like the empty evening. What should the second event be?
evals.expected_output: A recommendation to stay at one social occasion, with both promotion conditions evaluated separately and failing, and the upper options deleted from the menu and its axis orderings rather than ranked last.
expectations: Recommends staying at a single social occasion instead of choosing between the pub quiz and the walking tour
Names both conditions for moving up one rung - somebody actually asked for a second occasion, and a named owner exists for it - and evaluates them separately
States that either condition failing keeps the plan at one occasion
Identifies the user's own statement that nobody asked as the failing request condition
Identifies the same person owning both occasions as no owner for the second, because ownership is answered per occasion and never for the slate as a whole
Deletes the two-occasion and themed-track options from the menu rather than ranking them last or parking them as future options
States that the deletion applies to the effort, value, compliance-cost and efficiency orderings too, not only to the list of options
Names an empty hour in the evening as an illegitimate trigger for adding an occasion

evals.prompt: Quick count check for Aldergate Dev Summit. Our social programme for the week is: (1) our own welcome mixer Tuesday night, (2) an afterparty our platinum sponsor Vantik is throwing at a club on Wednesday, (3) a speakers-and-advisors dinner Wednesday, invitation only, 30 seats, (4) the local Rust user group's meetup Thursday, which is using our logo on their signup page. That's four social events, right? I want to put all four on the schedule page as our official social track and tell the code of conduct people we're covered. Give me the times to publish for each as well.
evals.expected_output: A slate of one occasion, the two third-party events routed to side-event coordination, the invite-only dinner routed to the invite-only gathering work, a non-overlap requirement instead of published times, and a handoff to the code of conduct.
expectations: Counts one occasion on the event's own slate, not four
Classifies the sponsor afterparty and the user-group meetup as events the organiser permits rather than provides, keeping both off the slate
Routes both third-party events to side-event coordination, including the logo usage on the user group's page
Hands the confirmed slate to side-event coordination as the calendar those third-party events are deconflicted against
Classifies the invitation-only speakers-and-advisors dinner as outside the open slate and routes it to the invite-only or named-guest gathering work
Declines to publish times for the occasions and states a non-overlap requirement for the schedule to place instead
States that placing or moving a slot belongs to the schedule, never to this decision
Hands the count and the places to the code of conduct so its scope clause reaches every occasion rather than only the one everybody remembered

evals.prompt: Hollins Tech Week, fourth edition, about 1,200 attendees. Our published accessibility commitments cover step-free access, a quiet alcohol-free space, childcare, and captioned content. We want a proper social track on Thursday evening: a run club, a board-game room, a family pizza hour, and a quiet crafting corner, all 18:00-21:00 across three different buildings. Our community manager Dara is fantastic and is happy to own all four of them. People come back partly for this stuff, it's part of why the event works. Green light?
evals.expected_output: A refusal to green-light the track as staffed, with all three track conditions evaluated separately, the single-owner condition identified as the failure, and the concurrency cost of three buildings named.
expectations: Declines to green-light the four-activity track as currently staffed
Names all three conditions the track requires - an access set no single format can carry at once, an owner per activity, and a recurring edition - and evaluates each separately
Identifies the diverse published access commitments and the recurring edition as the two conditions that are satisfied
Identifies one person owning all four activities as the failing condition, because the requirement is an owner per activity rather than one owner for the whole track
States that any one condition failing leaves the plan below the track
Describes a track held by a single owner as a sequence rather than a genuine track
Notes that the track's compliance cost rises with concurrency across more than one building, multiplying the access confirmation and the licensing question per place
Notes that a published track is expensive to withdraw once people have planned around it

evals.prompt: Northmoor Data Conf, 300 people, single day. We haven't decided anything about the evening yet. Honestly we might just do nothing and let people find a bar on their own. If we do put something on, rank the options for me: a mixer at the venue, a sit-down dinner with a programme, or a coach trip out to the old brewery. And if we end up doing two things, I'd want the dinner to be dry and the mixer to have beer on tap. Give me the ranking and say what each one serves.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to rank the three formats or to split the alcohol posture per activity, with both routed to the hospitality decision, plus the point that the do-nothing option sits there too and still has to be published.
expectations: Declines to rank the mixer, the sit-down dinner and the brewery trip itself, routing that ranking to the hospitality decision that owns the format menu
States that it produces no second, differently worded ranking of those same formats
States that the occasion format and the alcohol posture must already be decided before any slate depth is ranked
Refuses to give the dinner and the mixer different alcohol postures
States the alcohol posture is set once for the whole event, so a slate does not get a posture per activity
Routes the do-nothing option to the hospitality decision rather than treating it as a rung of the slate menu
States that the floor of the slate menu is one occasion
Notes that an absence still has to be published either way, because an unannounced absence sends people to an unhosted bar

evals.prompt: Braylin Open Source Days. The plan is to post a page on Monday listing six optional evening activities - pool night, escape room, open mic, city walk, board games, quiet lounge - and let attendees pick whichever suits them. More choice, more inclusive, right? The accessibility page with the venue details for each is coming the week after, our a11y volunteer is away until then. And if signups look thin on two of them we'll just quietly drop those. Write me the announcement copy.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to write the announcement, identifying the unqualified options list as a deleted option, rejecting publication before the access statement, rejecting the silent shortening, and requiring approval before further venues are held.
expectations: Refuses to produce the announcement copy as described
Identifies a slate published as a list of options with no statement of which one clears the access floor as a deleted option, not a lower-ranked one
Rejects the more-choice-is-more-inclusive reasoning, stating the choice is fake for exactly the people the floor exists for
States that a slate is not an access provision because it is long
Rejects publishing the slate before the access statement, because people plan around the slate the moment it appears
Notes that an access statement arriving later reaches only whoever is still deciding, which is not the population it was written for
Rejects quietly dropping activities after publication, stating that a published slate later shortened reads as a cancellation
Requires the slate to be presented for approval before any further venue is held

evals.prompt: Two questions for Sandhill Infra Con. First, we're running one big evening party this year instead of the three-activity thing we did last year, and my co-organiser keeps saying the single party is worth more because everybody is in the same room for once. Is she right, and how do I weigh that against reaching more people? Second, give me the benchmark numbers: what share of attendees should turn up to an official social activity, and how many activities per 500 attendees is normal? I want targets written into the plan before registration opens.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to supply attendance shares or activity-per-attendee ratios, slot floor coverage named as the only gate at zero uncovered slots, the rest self-set, and the shared-moment property confirmed as real but deliberately unranked.
expectations: Refuses to supply a benchmark attendance share for official social activities
Refuses to supply an activity count or a ratio of activities to attendees
Names slot floor coverage as the only gate, with the number being zero uncovered slots and no threshold applied
Marks the remaining measures as self-set and meaningful only across editions
Tells the user to pick one measure and write down before the event what it would change next edition
Confirms the co-organiser's shared-moment argument names a real property of a slate, while stating the menu deliberately does not rank it
States that the shared-moment property orders the options single occasion > two occasions on separate slots > themed track, and that this ordering is rank-identical to inverse effort
Says the co-organiser should argue for the shared moment directly rather than expecting the ranking to carry it
